method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: Total joint replacement in OA: indications, outcomes, complications, revision rates
topic.coverageNote: Indications for referral are grounded in NG226. Numeric outcomes, complication rates, and revision rates are not in this recommendations chapter and are not invented.

mcqs.question: When does NG226 say to consider referral for hip, knee, or shoulder replacement?

options.A: When symptoms substantially affect quality of life and non-surgical management is ineffective or unsuitable
options.B: At the first report of any joint pain, before exercise or analgesia
options.C: Only after a Kellgren-Lawrence grade is assigned on imaging
options.E: Never, because replacement is outside this guideline

mcqs.correctAnswerText: When symptoms substantially affect quality of life and non-surgical management is ineffective or unsuitable
mcqs.explanation: Consider referral if pain, stiffness, reduced function, or progressive deformity substantially affects quality of life and non-surgical care (exercise, weight loss, pain relief) is ineffective or unsuitable.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Consider referring people with hip, knee or shoulder osteoarthritis for joint replacement if: their joint symptoms (such as pain, stiffness, reduced function or progressive joint deformity) are substantially impacting their quality of life and non-surgical management (for example, therapeutic exercise, weight loss, pain relief) is ineffective or unsuitable.

mcqs.question: What should be used instead of a numerical severity score when deciding on referral?
mcqs.explanation: NG226 says to use clinical assessment when deciding to refer, instead of systems that numerically score disease severity.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Use clinical assessment when deciding to refer someone for joint replacement, instead of systems that numerically score severity of disease.

mcqs.question: Which factors must not be used to exclude someone from referral?

options.A: Age, sex or gender, smoking, comorbidities, and overweight or obesity including BMI
options.B: Only age; BMI is an absolute exclusion
options.C: Smoking is an absolute exclusion and the others are not mentioned
options.D: Comorbidity is required before referral can be considered
options.E: The guideline lists no equity statement

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Age, sex or gender, smoking, comorbidities, and overweight or obesity including BMI
mcqs.explanation: Do not exclude people because of age, sex or gender, smoking, comorbidities, or overweight or obesity based on measurements such as BMI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Do not exclude people with osteoarthritis from referral for joint replacement because of: age sex or gender smoking comorbidities overweight or obesity, based on measurements such as body mass index (BMI).

mcqs.question: What does NG226 say to explain about risk if referral is being discussed?

options.A: The risks of joint replacement can vary depending on age, sex, smoking, comorbidities, and obesity
options.B: Risk is identical for every patient
options.C: Risk cannot be discussed before surgery

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The risks of joint replacement can vary depending on age, sex, smoking, comorbidities, and obesity
mcqs.explanation: If discussing referral, explain that the risks of joint replacement can vary depending on the factors in recommendation 1.6.3.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If discussing referral for joint replacement, explain to the person with osteoarthritis that the risks of joint replacement can vary depending on the factors listed in recommendation 1.6.3.

mcqs.question: Does the NG226 recommendations chapter give revision-rate figures for hip or knee replacement?

options.A: No. It states referral indications and that risk varies, without publishing revision rates
options.B: Yes, a 2% ten-year revision rate for every implant
options.E: It reports a single national revision percentage that applies to all joints

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No. It states referral indications and that risk varies, without publishing revision rates
mcqs.explanation: The recommendations used here cover when to refer and what must not exclude referral. They do not publish revision rates, so no rate is taught from this chapter.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the risks of joint replacement can vary depending on the factors listed in recommendation 1.6.3
